text:
Iris: quick note from a customer call today — we hit confusing behavior around key rotation and env var names in our sampleapps. wanted to capture the short convo and agree next steps.

Iris: situation: customer rotated keys using our dashboard, but their running container (sampleapp) kept using the old org-scoped env var. they expected the SDK to detect rotation and prefer the rotated project-scoped credential we set.

Ben: concrete repro they gave: set REDWOOD_ORG_KEY=old_org_key and REDWOOD_API_KEY=new_proj_key, then curl to health route that calls SDK init. result: runtime picks old org key.

Sam: is the sampleapp caching the key at process start? we have prefix caching and many quickstarts call sdk.init() once then reuse client. rotation detection would need either signal (SIGHUP) or a short-lived refresh.

Priya: SDK behavior today: it reads env on init and caches into client instance. we intentionally avoided polling for env changes to prevent surprises. but for long-lived processes (workers), we should support a refresh helper and a documented pattern.

Iris: customer expectation was "rotate in dashboard -> app picks new key within minutes". we don't currently advertise that.

Ben: propose three-pronged approach: (1) quick UX doc clarifying rotation semantics for short-lived vs long-lived processes, (2) add a small SDK convenience: Client.refresh_from_env() which reloads env vars and validates token, (3) add a CLI helper `redwood auth rotate --notify <pid|service>` that either posts a SIGHUP or calls a small health endpoint to trigger refresh.

Sam: technical notes: refresh_from_env should be idempotent and optionally emit a WARN when token changed. also it should support an option `allow_fallback=false` to avoid silent fallthrough from PROJECT->ORG. By default keep fallback behavior but allow strict mode.

Priya: for parity: we must implement refresh_from_env in js/py/go/ruby and ensure precedence is consistent (we choose canonical order: REDWOOD_API_KEY > REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY > REDWOOD_ORG_KEY). also emit a one-time notice when legacy vars used.

Iris: I like canonical order. can we also add a small env normalization util in sdk-core used by all language wrappers to centralize logic? avoids code drift.

Ben: that's ideal but cross-language extraction is non-trivial. pragmatic plan: implement canonical spec in docs and copy a small reference implementation per SDK, plus a compliance test in CI that runs simple env combinations against each SDK and asserts consistent outputs.

Sam: timeline and owners? customer needs guidance this week.

Priya: timeline:
- short-term (48h): docs note in quickstart clarifying rotation behavior + sample SIGHUP handler for node/python. I'll PR docs and a sample supervisor script.
- medium (1 week): add refresh_from_env to SDKs (Priya + Ben), add unit tests for precedence, add a small e2e parity test in infra.
- long (1 month): CLI rotate helper + optional telemetry event when rotation detected (opt-in), and add deprecation warnings for legacy env names.

Iris: can telemetry be opt-in by org? some customers may not want signals about rotation.

Ben: yes, make it off by default; set via REDWOOD_OPT_IN_TELEMETRY=1 or console flag. keep payload minimal (just that a rotation/warn occurred, no token or identifier).

Sam: one UX ask: change our sampleapp quickstart to use REDWOOD_API_KEY only and update the container image to include a tiny sidecar that hits `/-/rotate` endpoint to trigger refresh. That gives customers a reference architecture.

Priya: agreed. I'll add a small example:
```
# in app startup
app.post('/-/rotate', (req, res) => {
  client.refresh_from_env({ allow_fallback: false })
  res.send('ok')
})
```

Iris: sounds good. please also add a troubleshooting snippet showing how to check which key the runtime currently uses: `redwood inspect-key --pid <pid>` or an equivalent endpoint that returns `source: REDWOOD_API_KEY` redacted.

Ben: I'll wire up `redwood inspect-key` in the CLI to call the app health endpoint if available, otherwise print envs from the process when run in the same container. make it safe and redact tokens.

migrations-bot: Created task RDW-5001: "Add Client.refresh_from_env() across SDKs + tests" (assignee: Priya).

Iris: thanks everyone. once short-term docs land I'll share with the customer. I'll coordinate with support to notify affected customers about the recommended container pattern and the new CLI helpers.

Priya: will push initial docs PR in next 24h and start SDK PRs after that.

Sam: nice work. small follow-up: add unit test that simulates dashboard rotation by swapping env file and hitting /-/rotate to ensure behavior is correct.

Iris: done. will follow up when PRs are up. :sparkles:
